October 11, 2026

Officials warn televised execution of Fort Hood shooter risks radicalization

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Law enforcement officials and lawmakers from both parties have condemned plans to publicly stream the execution of Nidal Hasan, who is in a wheelchair, warning that broadcasting it could radicalize viewers. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin responded to questions by saying people do not have to watch, and described the move as restoring American values. Some service members are reported to be seeking religious exemptions from participating.

Veteran HSI agent blames ICE hiring surge and training cuts for shootings

tags: immigration, policing
sources: @oafnation_actual

An anonymous Homeland Security Investigations agent said in a published interview that recent shootings by ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations branch stem from inadequate vetting, cut training and new enforcement mandates. The agent said officers had alternatives to engaging a target in New York City who had a child in his car, and criticized DHS Secretary Mullin for blaming the target. He also cited a July shooting in Maine in which an ERO surge hire with a history of domestic violence killed a man whose child was in the vehicle, and rejected Mayor Mamdani's call to abolish ICE.

Medicaid cuts drive wave of maternity ward closures

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Fifty-two maternity wards have closed across the United States in the past year, with eight more scheduled to close in the second half of this year, following federal Medicaid cuts enacted under last year's budget law. The closures are concentrated in rural and underserved hospitals that say they can no longer afford to operate the units. Women in affected areas face longer drives for maternity and emergency obstetric care.

Guilfoyle accused of asking GOP donor to wire her $100,000

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle allegedly asked Republican donor Eric Deters to pay off $100,000 in credit card debt in exchange for access to the Trump administration, six days before her July 2025 Senate confirmation hearing. Text messages reviewed by CBS News show her saying a wire to her American Express account would not show up publicly; Deters said he never sent the money and called the arrangement quid pro quo. Guilfoyle's attorney questioned the messages' authenticity and said prior payments were for appearances, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vice President JD Vance said they did not know the details.

FCC weighs letting AI political robocalls reach cellphones without consent

tags: politics, tech
sources: @groundnews

The Federal Communications Commission is considering a petition from Club for Growth to permit AI-generated political calls to cellphones without recipients' consent, arguing they should receive the same exemptions as automated bank and delivery notifications. The group, which plans to spend $175 million on November's congressional elections, says human operators initiate the calls before AI agents conduct interviews. Democratic Commissioner Anna Gomez and consumer advocacy groups urged rejection, warning voters could be flooded with calls before Election Day; public comment remains open until October 19.

Monitored wildlife populations fell 73% since 1970

tags: climate, environment
sources: @groundnews

Wildlife populations monitored worldwide declined by an average of 73% between 1970 and 2022, according to the World Wide Fund for Nature's 2026 Living Planet Report, which tracked 35,803 populations across 5,790 species. Freshwater populations saw the steepest average decline at 85%, followed by land species at 69% and marine species at 59%, with South America down 95% and Africa 80%. Habitat destruction was the most reported threat, alongside climate change, pollution and overexploitation; researchers noted the figure reflects average population declines rather than the share of individual animals lost.

Louisiana police chief candidate faces child rape charges while running unopposed

tags: policing, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Christopher Paul, a Republican candidate for city police chief in Elizabeth, Louisiana, is running unopposed after the only other candidate withdrew. He currently faces two counts of second-degree rape relating to allegations involving two 13-year-old girls about 20 years ago, with a complaint filed in August of this year. Some residents have called for the position to be changed from elected to appointed.

Trump administration removing more than 500 trees at East Potomac Park

tags: environment, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration has begun cutting down upwards of 500 trees at the East Potomac Golf Course in Washington, D.C., according to reporting by The Washington Post. The National Park Service says the removals are part of an effort to restore the site, while residents on the ground say the oaks, maples and other trees being felled are healthy rather than dying or invasive. The work has drawn anger from residents across the city.
